regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters. Decompose it: GVA growth trails by a statistical margin that historically reflects deflator choices, not real output gains. The honest proxies are more nuanced — PMI Composite at 55.9 recovered from 54.3 but remains below its six-month peak of 56.5, and core sector at 4.8% YoY is decelerating from 5.0%. The growth is real but narrowing: IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY is doing the heavy lifting while consumption proxies — PV sales falling two consecutive months to 7.9% YoY, CV sales falling to 12.6% YoY — suggest the demand base is thinning beneath the headline.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 5.54% YoY is the wrong number to watch. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is the number the RBI actually targets — and it sits 160 bps below headline, which means the spike is food and fuel, not embedded demand-pull. Food inflation at 7.74% YoY is rising two consecutive months; fuel at 22.93% YoY is a 95th-percentile print driven not by Brent — which has fallen five consecutive periods to $92.18/bbl — but by INR at 94.34, the 89th percentile. The inversion: global oil is falling, yet India's fuel inflation is accelerating. The rupee is the transmission mechanism, and it is not cooperating.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY sounds manageable — until you note that three months ago credit was 13.8% YoY and deposits were 9.9% YoY. The gap is widening in absolute terms even as the CD ratio edges down from 83% to 81%. NBFCs, unable to access bank funding at scale, are turning to corporate bonds at ₹18,700 cr / month — the 4th percentile historically — signalling rationing, not choice. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% while credit was accelerating, the regulator responded with risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending. The incentive to do so again is building.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, and the RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY implies a real rate of roughly 14 bps — barely positive. With fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY and food at 7.74% YoY, the RBI is threading a needle: cut and risk imported inflation feeding back through a weakening rupee; hold and watch credit stress compound in the NBFC sector. The Fed at 3.88% p.a. and rising, BOJ at 1.25% p.a. at a 15-year high, and US 10Y at 4.88% yield collectively narrow the RBI's room to ease without triggering FII outflows that are already at -₹49,935 cr net / month.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY, rising from 16.1%, and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% and now at the 68th percentile — is the cleanest signal of a genuine investment upcycle. The 75% threshold matters: below it, private capex is speculative; above it, it is rational. Iron ore at $161.91/t, up sharply from $92.71/t, confirms steel demand from construction and manufacturing, not just financial positioning. The risk to invert: if the credit squeeze tightens funding costs for mid-tier industrials, the capex cycle becomes a large-cap phenomenon while the broader investment multiplier stalls.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is a 74th-percentile print, but the composition matters more than the level. Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY — a mass-market, rural-sensitive indicator — are recovering, while PV sales at 7.9% YoY are decelerating for two consecutive months and CV sales at 12.6% YoY are falling. The divergence maps cleanly onto India's dual economy: rural informal demand (two-wheelers) is recovering, urban formal discretionary (PVs, CVs) is softening. GST's strength likely reflects formalization deepening rather than a broad demand surge — the kind of reclassification that flatters the aggregate without improving household balance sheets.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 71st percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 56th percentile. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month — 4th percentile, signalling NBFCs and mid-tier corporates are rationing bank credit and turning to capital markets.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and deposit franchises in metros — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will rise as CD ratio stays elevated. Expect RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher CRR exemptions, VRRR tweaks) within 2 months. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut in H2 FY27 if credit-deposit divergence persists.","pct_10y":71,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 71st percentile has preceded 2-3 quarters of NBFC stress and selective bank NPA upticks. Last time CD was this tight (2022-23), RBI eased liquidity and smaller banks saw deposit flight.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY — 53rd percentile. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest), up from 75.6% — 68th percentile, now in the sweet spot for fresh capex. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5% YoY but still positive). Iron ore prices at $161.91 / t, up sharply from $92.71 / t (prev), signalling strong demand from steel mills and construction. Nifty 50 up 4 of last 5 periods, now at 25,044.65 index (85th percentile).","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Accumulate positions in EPC contractors (L&T, Kalpataru, Patel Engineering) — order books will expand as PSU and private capex accelerates. Expect 12-18 month lag before IIP capgoods translates to earnings; lock in valuations now. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex cycle crowds out consumption.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the highest in 3 years and historically precedes 2-3 quarters of strong capex ordering. Last time CU was this high (2021-22), capex growth peaked at 25%+ YoY.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit All-Time High, But Ticket Size Rising","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,490 ₹ cr / month (latest), rising 3 consecutive months (29,845→31,961→32,297→32,490 ₹ cr / month) — 95th percentile. SIP accounts at 10.0646 mn (latest), but SIP AUM at 17.86 ₹ lakh cr — implying average ticket size of ₹17.75 lakh per account, up from ₹16.64 lakh cr / 10.45 mn = ₹15.9 lakh 3 months ago. Equity MF net inflows at 38,307 ₹ cr net / month (latest), up from 29,329 ₹ cr net / month — 85th percentile. DII equity net at 51,829 ₹ cr net / month (96th percentile) vs FII equity net at -49,935 ₹ cr net / month (14th percentile).","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour: mass retail SIP is plateauing (10.7% YoY growth, 31st percentile), but affluent money is entering via larger tickets. Rotate from small-cap SIP beneficiaries (Paytm, Zomato) to large-cap quality (HDFC Bank, TCS, Reliance). Expect SIP growth to decelerate to single digits by Q3 FY27. Domestic flows are masking FII outflows; be cautious on valuations above 22x Nifty P/E.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 95th percentile have historically preceded market corrections of 8-12% within 3-6 months. The last peak (2021) was followed by a 20% drawdown in 2022.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"watch","title":"Oil Collapse Masks Fuel Inflation Spike","data_text":"Brent crude at $92.18 / bbl (latest), down from $113.4 / bbl 5 months ago — falling 5 in a row. WTI at $86.53 / bbl, also down 5 consecutive periods. Yet fuel inflation in India at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% YoY — 95th percentile, a strong-negative signal. This divergence reflects INR depreciation (INR/USD at 94.34 ₹, up from 93.46 ₹ one month ago, 89th percentile) offsetting global oil price declines. Natural gas at $3.314 / MMBtu, up from $2.88 / MMBtu 3 months ago.","implication":"Fuel inflation will persist even if Brent stays at $90-95 / bbl because INR weakness is the transmission channel. RBI will struggle to cut rates; expect CPI to stay above 5% through Q3 FY27. Hedge INR exposure; avoid long INR positions. Overweight oil refiners (IOCL, BPCL) — they benefit from INR depreciation and lower crude costs. Underweight airlines and logistics (high fuel cost pass-through risk).","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has preceded RBI rate cuts being delayed by 1-2 quarters. In 2022, fuel inflation at 25%+ kept RBI on hold for 6 months despite core CPI moderating.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Breaks Carry Trade Calm","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (latest), up from 0.75% p.a. 3 months ago — 100th percentile, the highest in 15 years. Fed funds rate at 3.88% p.a., up from 3.75% p.a., rising 3 in a row (3.63→3.75→3.88% p.a.). ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a., up from 2% p.a. 3 months ago. US 10Y Treasury yield at 4.88% yield (latest), up from 4.84% yield — 89th percentile. US PMI Composite at 58.4 index (80th percentile), signalling US growth resilience. Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,327.87 index (100th percentile), but Nikkei 225 at 60,706.84 index (100th percentile) — both at all-time highs despite policy divergence.","implication":"Carry trade unwind risk is rising: JPY strength will force deleveraging of yen-funded positions. Expect 5-8% correction in global equities if BOJ signals further tightening. Reduce leverage; trim long positions in high-beta emerging markets. Overweight JPY and CHF (safe havens). Underweight INR and other EM currencies — they will weaken as carry trades unwind. Position for a 200-300 bps widening in US-Japan rate differentials by Q2 2026.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"BOJ at 100th percentile (highest in 15 years) has historically preceded 10-15% EM currency depreciation and 8-12% equity corrections within 2-3 months. The 2023 carry trade unwind saw Nikkei fall 20% in 3 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates Despite RBI Intervention","data_text":"INR/USD at 94.34 ₹ (latest), up from 93.46 ₹ one month ago — 89th percentile, weakest in 15 years. FII equity net at -49,935 ₹ cr net / month (latest), a sharp reversal from +29,631 ₹ cr net / month 2 months ago (14th percentile). DXY at 102.266 index (56th percentile), stable but elevated. US 10Y Treasury yield at 4.88% yield (89th percentile) is attracting capital away from India. Gold in INR at 12,248 ₹ / g (latest), up from 11,938 ₹ / g 5 months ago — 100th percentile, reflecting INR depreciation and safe-haven demand.","implication":"RBI is likely intervening to slow INR depreciation, but reserves are being drawn down. Expect INR to test 95-96 ₹ / USD within 2 months if FII outflows persist. Importers should hedge; exporters should lock in gains. Avoid long INR positions. Overweight gold and USD-denominated assets. Expect RBI to signal FX intervention limits and potentially raise rates by 25 bps in Q4 FY26 to defend the currency.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weakness has preceded 2-3 quarters of import compression and current account stress. In 2022-23, INR weakness to 82-83 ₹ / USD forced RBI to tighten and delayed rate cuts by 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pullback","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down from 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter 2 quarters ago — a 79% collapse, now at 0th percentile (lowest on record). Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (latest), down from 14.5% vacant, but this masks a bifurcated market: Grade A (GCC-occupied) vacancy rising, Grade B/C (traditional IT services) vacancy falling. Nifty IT index flat YoY despite Nifty 50 up 9% — IT services are not the office absorption driver. Yet Nifty 50 at 25,044.65 index (85th percentile) and Bank Nifty at 59,741.25 index (99th percentile) are at all-time highs. This divergence suggests: (1) GCCs (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple) are consolidating footprints and reducing headcount, not expanding; (2) traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shedding office space; (3) commercial real estate is decoupling from the IT stock proxy.","implication":"Sell commercial real estate REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) — they are overexposed to IT services and GCC consolidation. The 'office recovery' narrative is broken. Expect 15-20% REIT price declines over 12 months as absorption stays depressed and cap rates rise. Overweight residential real estate (home loan disbursements at 19,900 ₹ cr / quarter, up from 15,920 ₹ cr / quarter) and logistics warehouses (not exposed to IT). Avoid IT services stocks on valuation — they are not benefiting from office demand.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile (lowest on record) has never been sustained; historically, it rebounds within 2-3 quarters. However, the structural shift to hybrid work and GCC consolidation suggests this cycle is different — absorption may stay depressed for 4-6 quarters.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But the Demand Base Is Bifurcating

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY, PMI Composite at 55.9 — both above long-run medians, with IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY driving the investment leg.
  • But PV sales fell to 7.9% YoY (second consecutive monthly decline) and CV sales to 12.6% YoY — urban discretionary demand is losing altitude.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural informal recovery, while core sector at 4.8% YoY is decelerating from 5.0% — the goods economy is not keeping pace with the headline.
  • CPI at 5.54% YoY against core CPI at 3.9% YoY — the 160 bps gap is food and fuel noise, not demand-pull; but it keeps the RBI anchored.

The tension: Capex and rural demand are accelerating while urban consumption and goods output decelerate — a split economy where the headline GDP masks which half is actually driving growth.

Bottom line: Watch CV sales as the leading indicator of urban demand health; a third consecutive monthly decline would confirm the consumption softening is structural, not seasonal.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Acceleration Meets EM Tightening — India Caught in the Cross-Current

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR accelerated to 3.4% SAAR (from 2.2%), US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) — the US economy is re-accelerating, not slowing.
  • But BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest in 15 years) is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded EM equity inflows for a decade.
  • Fed funds at 3.88% p.a., rising three consecutive periods, with US 10Y at 4.88% yield (89th percentile) — the risk-free rate is competing directly with India's equity risk premium.
  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,328 (100th percentile) and Nikkei at 60,707 (100th percentile) — DM equities at all-time highs while FII equity net flows into India sit at -₹49,935 cr net / month.

The tension: DM growth re-acceleration is tightening global financial conditions precisely when India needs foreign capital to fund a widening current account — the two forces are pulling in opposite directions.

Bottom line: BOJ's next rate decision is the underappreciated tail risk; a move to 1.5% p.a. would accelerate yen carry unwind and amplify FII outflows from India within 30–60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Liquidity Holds — But the Architecture Is Fragile

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (95th percentile), rising three consecutive months — DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr net / month (96th percentile) is absorbing FII selling.
  • But MF AUM fell to ₹82.64 lakh cr from ₹87.08 lakh cr — mark-to-market erosion is shrinking the pool even as flows hold.
  • Average SIP ticket size rose to ₹17.75 lakh per account from ₹15.9 lakh three months ago — inflow growth is concentrated in wealthier accounts, not broadening participation.
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (4th percentile) — NBFCs rationing bank credit are not finding the capital markets as an easy substitute.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are providing a structural floor for equities, but the liquidity is increasingly concentrated — rising ticket sizes signal affluent savers, not mass participation — making the floor narrower than the aggregate suggests.

Bottom line: If MF AUM falls below ₹80 lakh cr on further mark-to-market pressure, redemption risk rises and the DII absorption buffer thins materially.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

REITs Price Office Collapse; Housing Narrows to a Shrinking Buyer Pool

The facts:

  • NRI buying is FALLING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (down 2 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%; the segment most exposed to INR depreciation and global carry-trade reversal is losing its marginal buyer.
  • Affordability index at 2.3× price ÷ income (5th percentile, 10-year low) — Hyderabad leads with sales up 15% YoY and launches up 120% YoY, but 28 months of unsold inventory signals supply is running ahead of demand.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter — down 79% from 19.5 mn sq ft two quarters ago — with GCCs at 42% of occupier mix consolidating, not expanding.
  • Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down 10–17% from prior prints, pricing the office demand collapse that the Nifty 50 at 25,045 has not yet acknowledged.

The tension: Equities at 85th-percentile valuations and Bank Nifty at a 99th-percentile 59,741 are pricing a growth cycle; REITs and affordability data are pricing a demand squeeze. One of them is wrong.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until GCC leasing data shows two consecutive quarters of absorption above 10 mn sq ft / quarter; the current 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter is not a trough — it is a reset.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — INR Is the Common Thread

The facts:

  • FII outflows at -₹49,935 cr net / month (14th percentile) with INR at 94.34 ₹ (89th percentile) — if outflows sustain, RBI intervention depletes reserves and the rupee overshoots, feeding fuel inflation further.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) unwinding carry trades — every 25 bps BOJ hike historically correlates with 2–3% EM currency depreciation within 60 days; INR has limited buffer.
  • CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits with credit at 19.4% YoY — if deposit growth stalls, the RBI's macro-prudential toolkit (risk weights, LCR tightening) gets deployed, compressing bank NIMs and triggering Bank Nifty derating.
  • But food inflation at 7.74% YoY rising two consecutive months — if the FAO Food Index at 136 (63rd percentile) continues rising, the RBI's rate-hold stance becomes untenable before Q1 FY28.

The tension: Each risk is individually manageable; the danger is sequencing — BOJ hike triggers INR weakness, which amplifies fuel and food inflation, which forces RBI to tighten precisely when credit stress is building.

Bottom line: Watch INR/USD: a sustained breach of 95.50 ₹ this week would signal RBI reserve depletion and force a policy response that equity markets have not priced.

"}
